units.text: Start with the measurement panel on the left. Identify whether CPU, memory, storage or networking limits the workload. Choose compatible instance features from representative measurements rather than a family name alone.

Follow the external database into the three Availability Zones. Keep durable state outside replaceable instances and design each dependency for its required resilience. Multiple compute locations alone do not make the data layer resilient.

Move to the demand curve and purchasing checklist. Select capacity purchasing and scaling policies around demand variation, startup delay and interruption tolerance. Test whether additional instances become useful before the workload exceeds its latency target.
With the full slide visible, use the final panel as an acceptance test. Exercise normal traffic, bursts, scale-in and failures, then check latency, cost, data safety and recovery together.
